headline: Apple owes record $5.7B in haptic tech patent case, US jury rules
summary: A US jury has ordered Apple to pay $5.7 billion in damages to a patent holder over haptic feedback technology used in iPhones.
details: A US jury has ruled that Apple must pay a record $5.7 billion in damages to a patent holder.
The case involves allegations that Apple infringed on patents related to haptic feedback technology, commonly used for vibrations in smartphones.
The technology in question is reportedly used in various iPhone models, providing tactile feedback to users.
This verdict represents one of the largest patent infringement awards in recent history.

headline: Apple ordered to pay $5.7 billion for patent infringement
summary: A jury found Apple's Taptic Engine infringed on two patents held by Taction, a company specializing in haptic feedback technology.
details: Apple has been ordered to pay a staggering $5.7 billion in a patent infringement case brought by Taction, a company that develops audio and gaming peripherals with haptic feedback.
Taction sued Apple in 2021, alleging that the Taptic Engine technology used in iPhones and Apple Watches violated two of its patents related to haptic feedback.
The lawsuit, initially dismissed in 2023, was revived by the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. A federal jury determined that Apple unintentionally infringed on Taction's patents.
This verdict represents one of the largest patent infringement payouts in US history, surpassing a $3 billion case involving Intel.
Apple has stated that it disagrees with the jury's decision and the awarded damages, and plans to appeal the verdict.
This is not the first time Apple has faced patent infringement claims regarding its haptic technology. The company previously settled an undisclosed amount with Immersion for similar allegations.
caption:
Apple faces a record-breaking $5.7 billion verdict for patent infringement related to its Taptic Engine technology.

Apple has been ordered to pay a staggering $5.7 billion in a patent infringement case brought by Taction, a company that develops audio and gaming peripherals with haptic feedback.

Taction sued Apple in 2021, alleging that the Taptic Engine technology used in iPhones and Apple Watches violated two of its patents related to haptic feedback.

The lawsuit, initially dismissed in 2023, was revived by the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. A federal jury determined that Apple unintentionally infringed on Taction's patents.

This verdict represents one of the largest patent infringement payouts in US history, surpassing a $3 billion case involving Intel.

Apple has stated that it disagrees with the jury's decision and the awarded damages, and plans to appeal the verdict.

This is not the first time Apple has faced patent infringement claims regarding its haptic technology. The company previously settled an undisclosed amount with Immersion for similar allegations.
